Before you get drunk on the headlines, let me walk you through the actual mechanics.

Under General License HH, shipping entity Roxette Maritime Shipping and Trading S.A. and seven associated vessels got slapped onto the SDN list today.

Concurrently, General License GG authorizes all transactions ordinarily incident and necessary to the wind-down of transactions involving 'Karnakis and Karnakis' or any entity owned 50% or more, directly or indirectly, by them ("Karnakis and Karnakis Entities").

The newly designated, sanctioned hulls under Roxette Maritime are: ANEMOS (IMO: 9205952), GLORIS (IMO: 9449510), PRIDE (IMO: 9487407), DESTINY (IMO: 9385491), FLAMINGO 1 (IMO: 9474199), HARMONY (IMO: 9449522), and PRINCE (IMO: 9548316).

Through this GL HH, the following narrow carve-outs are authorized:

1) Offloading at destination is permitted strictly for non-Iranian cargoes that were already loaded aboard these hulls prior to October 21.

2) Essential humanitarian provisions necessary to maintain the health, safety, and lives of the crew on board remain permitted.

3) Emergency marine repairs and environmental containment/salvage operations arising in transit are cleared.

4) The hard sunset on all safe-harbor activities is November 20, 2026. Any discharge or operational activity past this cutoff will be treated as outright illicit, triggering secondary sanctions risk.

5) This is strictly a damage control exit window. Fixing new charters or lifting fresh stems with designated entities is categorically prohibited.

6) Entering into new commercial agreements involving property or interests in property of blocked persons remains banned. No transactions prohibited under ITSR—including dealings with Iran, the Government of Iran, or Iranian-origin goods/services—are authorized.

7) Any payments owed to blocked persons must be routed directly into blocked accounts under ITSR compliance.

The cargo loaded on the ship may not be the property of Roxette Maritime, but legitimate non-Iranian cargo belonging to general global trading companies or third-country buyers.

If OFAC dropped an absolute blackout on all vessel ops without a wind-down clause, innocent charterers would be left stranded with hundreds of millions of dollars of physical product rotting in the middle of the ocean with zero legal recourse.

This is textbook collateral damage control and maritime risk prevention. But of course, the broader peanut gallery is entirely too fucking lazy to read beyond the raw headline.

Watching tourists claim Washington is "sending a surrender signal to Tehran" or crying "TACO" is so laughably brain-dead it physically hurts.

Literally takes 1 minute to pull the actual OFAC annex and read the fine print.

https://t.co/D0buxQYZLl

https://t.co/ZopwwxT0Uq

Together, these factors are keeping refined-product prices elevated, with distillates near USD 200 per barrel and Morgan Stanley warning that fuel tightness could persist through mid-2027. Meanwhile, Vortexa estimates that around 9 mb/d of crude has left the Gulf so far this month, well below levels implied by the US government. Ahead of today's EIA petroleum inventory report, the API reported a 4.9-million-barrel decline in US crude stockpiles.

Metals: Gold drifted back towards USD 4,100 on Tuesday before recovering to trade around USD 4,126 this morning. Elevated energy prices continue to cloud the interest-rate outlook, with traders pricing in three 25-basis-point rate hikes by next July. Overall, bullion remains confined to a relatively narrow range, caught between macroeconomic headwinds and continued demand from investors seeking protection against fiscal and geopolitical risks. Key resistance remains around USD 4,230, while support continues to emerge below USD 4,100.

Agriculture: Wheat futures slumped to their lowest level since mid-August, trading near USD 6.40 per bushel, down 20% from the three-year high reached last month. Prices have come under pressure amid hopes that an agreement to ease tensions in the Black Sea region could unlock substantial quantities of wheat from Russia and Ukraine currently awaiting export. The prospect of additional supplies comes at a time when Southern Hemisphere harvests are adding further pressure to an already weakening market.
